purpose: Record published corrugated-board inputs and comparison targets for a native Matter instrument.
evidence_status: literature specification only; no measurements or simulations were performed for this manifest
preferred_slice: Published target: A-flute rotary indentation, orthotropic-elastic liner and medium option (a). The current initial Matter slice is a small end-grip bend instrument without contact or crease formation, so it is not yet a reproduction of the published crease protocol.
current_initial_matter_slice: Small end-grip bending instrument; no contact/creasing and no experimental validation claim.

sources.citation: Nagasawa, S.; Komiyama, Y.; Mitsomwang, P. Finite Element Analysis of Corrugated Board on Rotary Creasing Process. Journal of Advanced Mechanical Design, Systems, and Manufacturing 7(2), 103-114 (2013).

board.basis_weight_note: Component paper basis weights are reported; finished-board grammage is not. Do not sum flat-sheet grammages as finished-board grammage because flute take-up and adhesive mass are unreported.

default_material_model_a.description: Both liners and corrugated medium are orthotropic elastic; the source reports no fracture model.
default_material_model_a.source_ref: Table 3, printed p.105; shear moduli are said to follow the equations on printed p.105. Reverse Poisson ratios are not independently listed.
default_material_model_a.poisson_closure_assumption: The current material file reads the first subscript as the loading axis and derives reverse ratios by nu_ij/E_i=nu_ji/E_j. This is conventional but not explicitly defined in the paper.
default_material_model_a.source_shear_consistency_note: Under that axial-first closure, the printed shear-modulus equations give liner G_MT/G_TC/G_CM about 19.89/19.41/1061 MPa and medium about 15.92/15.57/1116 MPa, versus Table 3 values 20/20/1175 and 16/16/1250 MPa. Use the tabulated shear values directly and retain the closure as an implementation assumption; the paper is not fully self-consistent under this interpretation.

crease_model.edge_liner_boundary: both lateral edges fixed in the source default; free-edge case was also studied
crease_model.feed: source assumes sheet feed speed equals roller circumferential speed; with zero friction it imposes feed as a constraint
crease_model.declared_implementation_assumption: Use tied/perfect-bond interfaces for a first executable model because the paper gives no adhesive geometry or interface law. This is an assumption, not a calibrated source input.

published_profile_observables.profile_state: Source profile/stress plots report the worksheet front position s/t=-1.6; treat this as a source state label, not as an applied physical displacement.

alternate_rct_medium_model_c.description: Orthotropic-elastic liners plus isotropic-elastoplastic corrugated medium with Ring Crush Test equivalent properties.
alternate_rct_medium_model_c.hardening_law: not specified in sufficient detail for strict reproduction
alternate_rct_medium_model_c.use_limit: Keep as an alternate only. The RCT values act as effective crush/buckling response; combining them with an explicit flute geometry may count core buckling twice.

material_and_validation_limits: The model-a liner is elastic and does not fail; at the reported state its simulated liner strain is 0.036 versus measured raw-sheet breaking strain 0.014 (Section 4.1, printed p.110).
Model-a predicts a 163 degree crease angle versus a physical 124-132 degree range; its profile is not a deep-crease validation.
The source reports qualitative liner-failure locations, not a measured stress field or a quantitative failure threshold for the simulation.
The source does not report adhesive properties, an interface law, or an RCT hardening curve.

other_source_inputs.raw_sheet_test_source_ref: Tables 1-2, printed p.105; 10 samples; 24 h conditioning at 296 K and 50% RH
other_source_inputs.reported_raw_modulus_unit_note: Table 1 prints 5.02 and 1.88 under an MPa heading while Table 3 gives 5020 and 1884 MPa; retain Table 3 for FE inputs and treat the Table 1 unit/scale as internally inconsistent.

sources.citation: Aduke, R.N.; Venter, M.P.; Coetzee, C.J. Numerical Modelling of Corrugated Paperboard Boxes. Mathematical and Computational Applications 29(4), 70 (2024).
sources.role: Separate C-flute reference; do not combine its properties with the A-flute data above.

board.basis_weight_note: Component grammages only; actual finished-board grammage is unreported because flute take-up and adhesive contribution are not given.
board.geometry_note: Fig. 6 p.6 dimension 3.861 spans the inner liner faces. Subtract core thickness before using it as mid-surface peak-to-trough. Derived values are interpretations of the figure.

four_point_bending_target.geometry_caveat: The paper's labels/wording for the 200 mm and 340 mm anvil pairs should be checked against Fig. 4 before reproducing the fixture; do not silently swap their roles.

table5_values_as_printed.unit_caveat: Table 5 p.15 prints N/m, but Eq. (1) has dimensions of force times length. Preserve the published label and values; N*m is the dimensionally consistent interpretation, pending author confirmation.

model_notes.interface: Structural FE layers are connected by shared nodes at flute extremes (perfect tie); authors note this rigid connection can overestimate stiffness relative to flexible starch bonds.
model_notes.elements: Thick-shell; structural mesh 0.5 mm, homogenised mesh 2 mm; quarter symmetry; top rigid cylinder position-controlled downward; bottom cylinder static; no other boundary conditions stated.
model_notes.crease_representation: A 4 mm reduced-property strip calibrated from bending tests, not a simulated crease-forming process.
model_notes.data_availability: Raw data are available from authors on request; paper provides tabulated stiffness and plotted curves, not a public data file.

sources.material_source_refs: Table 1 p.7; Table 3 p.10; Table 4 p.15. Orthotropic elastic constants and yield values are recorded in sources.md; missing Hill strain ratios limit exact plastic reconstruction.

sources.citation: Beex, L.A.A.; Peerlings, R.H.J. An experimental and computational study of laminated paperboard creasing and folding. International Journal of Solids and Structures 46 (2009), 4192-4207.
sources.role: Scope boundary only: laminated solid paperboard, not a corrugated flute board; do not transfer its geometry or properties into either corrugated benchmark.
